description:
On November 10, 1963, Gordie Howe etched his name in NHL history as the all-time leading goal scorer. The remarkable feat occurred during a resounding 3-0 victory over the Montreal Canadiens. Widely known as "Mr. Hockey," Howe's 545th career goal surpassed the legendary Maurice "Rocket" Richard. The momentous occasion unfolded at Detroit's Olympia Stadium, where a crowd of 15,027 spectators erupted into a thunderous standing ovation lasting a remarkable 15-20 minutes to honor their hero. In the second period of the game, the play that led to the milestone goal transpired. Howe swiftly skated down the right side of the ice, positioning himself perfectly to receive a pass from Billy McNeil just inside the blue line. With precision and skill, Howe swiftly snapped the puck past goaltender Charlie Hodge, sending it low and just inside the right post for a sensational shorthanded goal. The celebration erupted as Howe's jubilant teammates flooded the ice, commemorating the historic moment in hockey.

description:
Teemu Selanne scored his third goal of the game during the third period, securing his record-setting 54th goal of the 1992-93 season. This impressive feat surpassed Mike Bossy's rookie record of 53 goals, which had been set fifteen seasons earlier. The play unfolded when Selanne's teammate, Tie Domi, launched the puck high into the air, landing near center ice. In a display of speed and skill, Selanne outpaced the defenseman, swatting a backhander past the sliding goalie to secure the record-breaking goal. The ice quickly filled with Selanne's jubilant teammates, celebrating his accomplishment. To commemorate the occasion, the team awarded Selanne a stick, which he raised towards the crowd at center ice in a gesture of gratitude. The rookie season for "The Finnish Flash" saw him tally an astounding 76 goals, obliterating the previous record and earning him the prestigious Calder Trophy.

description:
During the 1993-94 season, Wayne Gretzky achieved a historic milestone by surpassing his childhood idol, Gordie Howe, to become the NHL's all-time leading goal scorer. The remarkable play unfolded with Luc Robitaille spearheading the attack, entering the opposing zone and executing a drop pass back to Gretzky. Displaying his exceptional playmaking abilities, Gretzky swiftly delivered a pass to Jari Kurri, who in turn sent the puck over to Marty McSorley. Positioned unmarked on the left side, Gretzky received a pass from McSorley, allowing him to effortlessly tap the puck into the net for the goal. The electrified crowd erupted in cheers as the Kings' bench swiftly flooded the ice, celebrating this incredible accomplishment. The memorable moment came in Gretzky’s 15th NHL season, one in which “The Great One” led the League in both assists and points.

description:
In a defining moment of the 1991 Stanley Cup Final against the Minnesota North Stars, Mario Lemieux delivered a goal that would become iconic. This extraordinary play paved the way for the Pittsburgh Penguins to secure their first-ever Stanley Cup victory. With the Penguins holding a 2-1 lead late in the second period, Lemieux takes control of the puck deep in his own zone and swiftly sets off, building momentum as he moves up the ice. Crossing the blueline, Lemieux showcases his unmatched skill by gracefully maneuvering past two Minnesota defenders. With a quick shift of the puck onto his backhand, he expertly places it beyond the reach of goaltender Jon Casey. The goal not only showcased Lemieux's brilliance but also propelled the Penguins closer to their championship triumph. Throughout the playoffs, Lemieux displayed incredible prowess, leading to him being awarded the prestigious Conn Smythe Trophy. His exceptional performance included registering an impressive 44 points in just 23 games, ranking as the second-highest number of playoff points ever recorded in a single season in NHL history.

description:
On Dec. 23, 2022, Alex Ovechkin surpassed “Mr. Hockey,” Gordie Howe, for second place on the NHL’s all-time goals list behind “The Great One,” Wayne Gretzky. “The Great 8” has had a remarkable career having won the Maurice "Rocket" Richard Trophy on nine occasions – the most any NHL player has finished as single-season goals leader. Ovechkin tops a list of only three players to lead the League in goals more than five times, the others being Bobby Hull (7x) and Phil Esposito (6x). For his first goal of the game (801), the play begins with Ovechkin feeding the puck to teammate Ryan Strome on the far side in the neutral zone. As Strome gains the blue line, Ovechkin trails the play getting the drop pass where he walks it in and zips it five-hole past the netminder. In the final play, Ovechkin gains the blue line with the puck where he has a clear shot at the empty net. Instead, he pulls up and passes it over to longtime teammate Evgeny Kuznetsov. Kuznetsov dishes it back to Ovechkin where he spins alongside the boards and throws it into the empty net in front of an elated home crowd, with his teammates then flooding the ice in celebration.

description:
After an illustrious career spanning 22 seasons, Ray Bourque finally achieved the ultimate triumph of hoisting the Stanley Cup. At the age of 40, in what would be his final year in professional hockey, Bourque fulfilled his long-standing dream of winning this highly coveted trophy. This remarkable achievement added to the numerous accolades he had already earned, including holding the record for the most goals, assists and points in NHL history by a defenseman, along with five Norris Trophy awards. Leading up to this historic victory, Bourque showcased his invaluable contributions by scoring the game-winning goal during Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final. With the game tied and a power play in progress, a crucial faceoff ensued in the early moments of the third period. Bourque skillfully seized control of the puck after it was won back to him, swiftly gliding towards the center of the ice before unleashing a powerful slapshot that flew past the formidable Martin Brodeur. Then, on June 9, 2001, following a resounding 3-1 victory by the Colorado Avalanche in Game 7, team captain Joe Sakic received the coveted Stanley Cup from Commissioner Gary Bettman. In a deeply significant gesture, Sakic promptly skated over to Bourque, personally handing off the cherished trophy to the deserving veteran. This poignant moment served as the culmination of Bourque's extraordinary career, marking the pinnacle of his accomplishments and forever etching his name into hockey lore.
